result.topic_en: Rectification of the ellipse: computing the arc length integral $\int\sqrt{a^2\cos^2T+b^2\sin^2T}\,dT$ via the arithmetic-geometric mean, with a numerical example applied to the Earth's meridian quadrant.
result.transcription:
Math 25
Zur Rectification der Ellipse  (63)  [-47d-] 12
Es sei $\int \sqrt{(aa\cos T^2 + bb\sin T^2)}\, dT =$ [-...-] $W$
Man bilde die Reihe der arithm. geom. Mittel
$a, b$ | $aa-bb=16cc$ | $cc=a'c'$
$a', b'$ | $a'a'-b'b'=16c'c'$ | $c'c'=a''c''$
$a'', b''$ | $a''a''-b''b''=16c''c''$ | $c''c''=a'''c'''$
&c | &c. | &c.
$\vdots$
$\alpha$
Man hat dann ferner zu setzen
$\frac{4\sin T}{a}=p$  $cp=\sin 2u$  $p'=\frac{p}{\cos u^2}$
$\frac{4\sin T'}{a'}=p'$  $c'p'=\sin 2u'$  $p''=\frac{p'}{\cos u'^2}$
$\frac{4\sin T''}{a''}=p''$  $c''p''=\sin 2u''$  &c
$\vdots$  $\vdots$
Dann ist, den letzten Werth von $T=\Theta$ gesetzt
$W=\frac{\Theta}{\alpha}\{a'a'-32c''c''-64c'''c'''-128c^{iv}c^{iv}\ldots)$
$+8c'\cos T\sin T'+16c''\cos T'\sin T''+32c'''\cos T''\sin T'''+\ldots$
$=\frac{\Theta}{\alpha}(a'a'-32c''c''-64c'''c'''-128c^{iv}c^{iv}\ldots)$
$+2a'p'\cos T+4a''p''\cos T'+8a'''p'''\cos T''\ldots$
